labels: KV cache grows. Flash Attention keeps the hot path in SRAM.
KV cache — decoding step by step
each new query attends to N cached k/v — O(N) per step, not O(N²)
KV cache and Flash Attention are universal in 2026 — vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, llama.cpp all assume both.
Next frontier: PagedAttention (KV as virtual memory), prefix caching, speculative decoding.

=== attention mask shapes on an 8-token sequence ===

full causal  (36 / 64 cells attended)
   0 | x.......
   1 | xx......
   2 | xxx.....
   3 | xxxx....

   5 | xxxxxx..
   6 | xxxxxxx.
   7 | xxxxxxxx

sliding window (W=4)  (26 / 64 cells attended)
   0 | x.......
   1 | xx......
   2 | xxx.....
   3 | xxxx....
   4 | .xxxx...
   5 | ..xxxx..
   6 | ...xxxx.
   7 | ....xxxx

local (W=2) + strided (stride=3)  (24 / 64 cells attended)
   0 | x.......
   1 | xx......
   2 | xxx.....
   3 | x.xx....
   4 | x..xx...
   5 | x..xxx..
   6 | x..x.xx.
   7 | x..x..xx

=== attention sink: one 'noisy' query on 8 random tokens ===
single attn weights: 0.018 0.068 0.335 0.031 0.054 0.112 0.156 0.227
  (notice the weight bleeding to position 0 — the attention sink)
diff   attn weights: +0.008 +0.030 +0.169 +0.013 +0.033 +0.039 +0.097 +0.112
  (lambda=0.5 subtracts the sink component; negative weights allowed)

=== KV cache @ 128K context, Llama-3-70B-ish (80 layers, 8 KV heads, d_head=128, fp16) ===
  full attention              :   42.9 GB
  SWA window= 4096             :    1.3 GB   (32x shrink)
  SWA window= 1024             :    0.3 GB   (128x shrink)
  Gemma-3 mix (5:1, W=1024)   :    7.4 GB   (5.8x shrink)
  differential attention (2x) :   85.9 GB   (pays 2x for sink-free weights)

takeaway: SWA is the cheapest long-context win.
          Gemma 3's 5:1 mix keeps enough global layers for retrieval
          while shrinking KV ~6x vs pure full attention.
          DIFF attention pays 2x KV for sink-free, sharper retrieval.
